To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a sensitive mammalian cell reporter system was established to assess the DNA-binding activities of ZFNs, and the targeted chromosomal repair efficiencies of ZFNs were in proportion with the combinations of binding activities of their ZFLs and ZFRs.
a mammalian cell-based ZFP screening system with multiple TSF copies can be used to identify the ZFP candidates with low binding activities.
the mammalian cell-based luciferase reporter system is able to detect the low binding activities of ZFNs and can be used to screen the failed half-ZFNs for the rescue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the establishment of a highly sensitive mammal cell-based reporter system for the screening of ZFNs with high binding activities.
the development of a sensitive mammalian cell based reporter system for screening ZFP candidates with low DNA-binding activity.
the rescue of failed half-ZFNs by a sensitive mammalian cell based luciferase reporter system, which will help to optimize the ZFP candidates for ZFN generation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the screening of ZFNs by the mammalian cell-based luciferase reporter system can rescue failed half-ZFNs, which is an efficient method to generate functional ZFNs in a short period of time.
this paper establishes a highly sensitive mammal cell-based transcriptional luciferase reporter system to assess and rescue the DNA binding activity of a half-ZFN.

the screening sensitivity of the cell-based reporter system is up to 50 times that of the traditional EMSA assay and the binding activity of a ZFP is not necessarily a good predictor of its ability to form a functional ZFN pair.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rescue of a failed half-ZFN can be achieved by combining it with a high binding activity half-ZFP.
the failure ZFNs might be rescued by this sensitive mammalian cell based transcriptional reporter system.
the failed half-ZFNs could be rescued and the successful ZFNs could be further optimized to achieve a higher genome-editing efficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have established a highly sensitive and efficient mammalian cell-based ZFN screening system, which can be used to identify ZFN candidates among the failed ZFPs and improve the success rate of the ZFN generation.
a ZFP candidate with a low binding activity may be rescued by another binding active ZFP, which may provide an effective way for the generation of a biological active ZFP pair for genome editing.

a sensitive reporter system is a powerful tool for screening the DNA binding activities for ZFPs, and a ZFN pair with a high binding activity of one half-ZFP and a low binding activity of the other half-ZFN can be generated by combining a sensitive reporter system and a modular-assembly method.
